data.cultural_impact: The name Elia was popularized by the Spanish missionaries during the Spanish colonization of the Americas, as they used the Biblical name Elias as a given name for Christian children.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Elias is a reminder of God's presence and power, and the importance of staying true to one's faith in the face of opposition or temptation. Elias's story in the Bible is an enduring testament to the power of faith and God's faithfulness to His people.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Elias, meaning "God is my God," is a biblical name representing faith, devotion, and commitment to the divine. It is a name of strength and courage, reminding us to rely on God in times of challenge and adversity.

biblical_reference.note: Elijah is introduced as a prophet in the Old Testament

historical_references.reference: Elijah was a prophet in the Northern Kingdom of Israel during the reigns of Ahab, Jezebel, and Ahaziah. He is known for challenging the Baal prophets at Mount Carmel in a contest to determine whose god was the true God.
historical_references.context: During the time of the divided monarchy, Israel in the north and Judah in the south, Elijah was a major prophet in the northern kingdom. He opposed the worship of the Canaanite god Baal and led the people to recognize the sole sovereignty of Yahweh, God of Israel.

historical_references.reference: Elijah was taken up into heaven in a whirlwind in the presence of Elisha, his successor. This event is described in 2 Kings 2:11 and is considered a precursor to the ascension of Jesus into heaven.
historical_references.context: After a long ministry, Elijah was taken up into heaven in a chariot of fire, leaving Elisha to continue the prophetic work. This event was a significant one for the Jewish people and was later seen as foreshadowing the ascension of Jesus into heaven.
